messages:
Anya (support): Hey team, just escalated from a customer (they're on CloudFront -> NLB -> our private instance) — streaming completions are getting truncated mid-response and clients see a short reconnect loop. They say partial tokens are dropped (end of chunk missing) and replays add duplicate text.

Anya (support): Symptoms: SSE stream opens fine, we send ~12 tokens then connection closes from client side, client reconnects immediately and receives remaining tokens + repeated text. Happens more frequently when client is behind CloudFront TTL/idle settings.

Tim (se): Do we have any logs showing RST/FIN? Any 502/504?

Anya (support): No 502/504. Backend logs show stream completed server-side. TCP traces from customer show connection FIN from their edge after ~15s idle, but our process reports last bytes sent.

Alex (ops): Hmm this smells like NLB idle timeout + half-close behavior. NLB has a 350s default? But when CloudFront is in front it can speak HTTP/2 to CF and then CF->NLB might downgrade to HTTP/1.1 and do its own idle/window handling. Could be a FIN being sent with buffered chunk left in proxy that never makes it to client.

Maria (platform eng): Another possibility: CloudFront/edge does aggressive connection reuse/keep-alive termination if there is no data for X seconds. For SSE we rely on frequent small chunk flushes. If proxy buffers and collapses empty flushes, the client sees gap. Also if NLB is doing TCP half-close and the origin keeps writing after receiving FIN it can lead to RST on the origin side.

ingress-bot: Automated note: recent deploy 2067889000 changed nginx config on private cluster (proxy_buffering on). Rollback flag: false.

Tim (se): Can you get repro steps I can run locally? Prefer simple curl reproducible case with --no-buffer and a short heartbeat interval so we can emulate.

Anya (support): Customer provided repro curl: 
```
curl -v -N https://api.example.com/v1/stream?model=foo \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
```
They say after ~12 chunks it stops and then client reconnects.

Alex (ops): Try reproducing with an NLB in front using a small test service. Also test CloudFront in front (h2 -> h1 translation). Locally we can emulate with socat or a simple node sse server. Here's a quick node server we used before: 
```js
// sse-test.js
const http = require('http')
http.createServer((req,res)=>{
  res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'Connection': 'keep-alive' });
  let i=0;
  const t = setInterval(()=>{
    res.write(`data: token-${i}\\n\\n`);
    i++;
    if(i>20){ clearInterval(t); res.end(); }
  }, 2000);
}).listen(3000)
```
Then hit it through the same LB setup.

Maria (platform eng): Important checks: 
- Are we sending proper chunked Transfer-Encoding headers?
- Are proxies doing any gzip or response buffering? (nginx has proxy_buffering, proxy_request_buffering)
- TCP keepalive vs application heartbeats.

Tim (se): Add some quick curl tests: 
```
# no buffering, verbose
curl -v --no-buffer http://localhost:3000/ | sed -u 's/^/CLIENT: /'
# simulate slow consumer
perl -e 'sleep 20' | nc -q 1 localhost 3000
```

Anya (support): Customer also sent a pcap showing FIN from CloudFront -> NLB after ~14s of inactivity on that connection. Our instance still had bytes in its socket send buffer. After FIN, origin saw RST when trying to write more data.

Alex (ops): That aligns with 'write after half-close' causing RST. Fixes: ensure proxies don't close idle connections so aggressively, or send frequent SSE keepalives (a comment/empty event) < interval. For NLB specifically, tune idle timeout (AWS NLB default is 350s for TCP, but CloudFront might force shorter). For CloudFront, increase origin keep-alive timeout and use HTTP/2 end-to-end if possible.

Maria (platform eng): We should also disable response buffering on our nginx ingress for SSE endpoints. Example config snippet: 
```nginx
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_set_header Connection '';
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
}
```
Also ensure `proxy_request_buffering off;` on POST endpoints that stream.

Tim (se): Another workaround: application-level heartbeat every 10s: send `: keepalive\\n\\n` (comment event) so upstream proxies see activity and the edges don't tear down.

Anya (support): Customer asked if we can detect this server-side and retry/resume. Right now we don't have idempotent final-state resumes for streaming responses; we'd need to implement the delta token replay on reconnect. That's non-trivial.

Alex (ops): Short-term remediation for customer: 
- Put ALB instead of NLB where possible (ALB handles HTTP/1.1/2 better for SSE and has idle timeouts you can configure on listeners).
- If must use NLB, configure client-facing CloudFront/edge to longer origin keepalive and set Origin Response headers: `Connection: keep-alive` and disable HTTP/2 if translation causes issues.
- Disable gzip on streaming route.
- Add app heartbeat every 10s.

Maria (platform eng): Action items: 
1) Support to gather pcap + tcpdump from customer (we have their permission).
2) Ops to spin up a test in staging that mirrors CF -> NLB -> ingress with same nginx config.
3) Platform to add ingress annotation template to disable proxy_buffering for stream endpoints and docs for customers.
4) SE to provide sample heartbeat patch for client libraries.

Tim (se): I'll write a small patch for our node/python SDKs that sends a keepalive comment and does a linear backoff on reconnect to avoid duplicate token spam.

Anya (support): Customer responded: happy with workaround steps, can test heartbeat and try switching to ALB. They've requested we prioritize a docs KB.

Alex (ops): Noted. I'll also check deploy diff for 2067889000 to see why proxy_buffering was turned on. Might be a global change that caught streaming endpoints.

Maria (platform eng): Logging note: we should add an event log entry when the server writes after socket FIN/RST — currently it's swallowed. That will help triage similar cases.

Anya (support): Thanks all — I'll collect logs/pcap and open a ticket with attachments. Keeping this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
